decisions: Inspected all 17 merges and 52 routes, the nine substantive edits and the four retirements. C03 remains a narrow legal-coverage dispute, with Privacy Act and privilege limits. Methods and undercover-officer facts have no extra vote. Generic empathy, information access and possible misuse do not establish Tolerance; documented group blame remains distinct.
source_context_read: Targeted passages of FOIA/Privacy Act materials, Brown/Clemente and the law-enforcement-privilege opinion, secrecy evidence and value-linked examples; no new live retrieval.

merges.decision: Direct text of the bill, verified against the packet bill text. Background only; it is not a judgment on any complete argument.

The list and its limits are direct text; the absences are checked by reading the complete list. This claim does not decide whether other laws, such as the Privacy Act, also apply; that question is in C03 and in local qualifications.

Four active arguments need this risk premise and no more. Two things make it a judgment: the responses on UNC_oppose_03, SEP_oppose_01 and SES_oppose_01 say other law protects source names, and whether protections outside the bill cover all such secrecy is a specific unresolved legal gap. No packet passage read decides it. Editorial issues on SES_oppose_01 and UNN_oppose_02 record the premise as unresolved. A universal version (every source must be exposed) is not needed by any user and is not claimed.

substantive_edits.reason: Clarified wording. Response narrowed to one defective step: payment data to conservation results and current choices. Dropped “no lesson they add for judging an active conservation effort” as a separate demand, moved the earlier public warning to the later strength comparison as a baseline fact, and added an explicit concession that spending can be checked. Sources unchanged.

Removed the blanket response under editorial issue HR4405_UNN_oppose_02: a measured bill-specific change or a named environmental informant is not required, and unchanged protection for unrelated files does not alone rebut a reputational spillover. Preserved those scope facts as a Note in the support, citing the same bill text and FOIA sources. The exposure premise stays separately disputed in shared claim C03. No-response marker now applies.

Plain “people who secretly helped investigators” in title; “FOIA” explained as public-records law; quotations unchanged. Response now states its reach: names the Privacy Act protects, not other source information or people it does not cover, so that it matches the rescoped risk premise in C03.

Applied editorial issue HR4405_UNT_support_03. Cut the political-opponents and listening branch, plus the political-embarrassment bullet that served it. The response targeted only that cut branch and said it did not address the collective-blame branch, so it has no remaining target: no-response marker now applies. NPR’s speculation quotation left with the response. Mixed-effects note stays visible in support.

Applied editorial issue HR4405_UNT_oppose_02. Title and argument made specific to documented exploitation for antisemitic collective blame. Omitted the less directly supported political-group extension and NPR quotation. The absence of a measured change in beliefs or audience is routed to strength by main adjudication, not added to support. “Massie–Khanna” glossed. No general rule against publishing misusable information. No-response status preserved.

Clarified wording. Narrowed the response: removed the demand to identify a person or a finding of continuing abuse, and treated the New Mexico inquiry as supporting an earlier step. Retained the actual defect: contrary evidence on the step from inquiry to protection. Same sources.

Explained source, inspector general and House memo; simplified the legal canon; quotations unchanged. Response narrowed to names the Privacy Act protects and now states what it leaves unaddressed, so that it matches the rescoped risk premise in C03.
Clarified wording. Response restated around contrary evidence on one step, so that it does not imply a certainty requirement. Same sources.

Applied editorial issue HR4405_SES_oppose_01. Removed the blanket “does not connect this limited release to less cooperation” allegation from the Response and the So. Moved the point about other grand juries to a support Note. Added from the same August 2025 opinion that the agent gave hearsay accounts of select witnesses, so the Maxwell fact is not overread, and stated that the fact covers Maxwell only. Source-identity objection kept on its own evidence and limited to names the Privacy Act protects, matching the rescoped risk premise in C03.
